# TDPdf v1.19.0.0

A fork-sync release pulling the newest useful features and fixes from upstream [**SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF**](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF) (v1.6.5 and v1.6.6) and adapting them to TDPdf's diverged multi-tab architecture. This build ships everything merged to `main` since the last release, headlined by the changes below. See [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/doodlemania2/TDPdf/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the complete per-version history.

As always: this fork only exists because upstream KillerPDF is a genuinely great, dark-themed, no-telemetry, no-cloud Windows PDF editor. **Go star [the upstream project](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF).**

## Highlights

### Text selection that follows the text (new in 1.19.0.0)
Dragging with the Select tool now tracks the actual run of characters in reading order — across lines and paragraphs, browser-style — instead of sweeping up whatever fell inside a rectangle. **Ctrl+A** shows real per-line selection.

**Highlight** follows the text the same way: drag across words and the markup hugs each line. Two new tools join it — **Strikethrough** and **Underline**. One drag produces one annotation that selects, moves, deletes and undoes as a single unit.

A plain click still selects annotations, a drag starting on blank page still box-selects, and **Shift+drag** always forces the classic marquee.

> Selection works in Single, Two-Page and Grid view on the active page. Continuous view keeps the previous behavior — see *Known gaps* below.

### Tool shortcuts, finally (new in 1.19.0.0)
TDPdf had no tool hotkeys at all. Now the digits mirror the toolbar left to right, with mnemonic letters alongside:

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| **V** Select | **5** / **H** Highlight | **9** / **D** Draw | **G** Signature |
| **P** Pan | **6** / **K** Strikethrough | **0** / **E** Erase | **C** Crop |
| **1** / **T** Text | **7** / **U** Underline | **4** / **I** Insert Image | |
| **2** / **X** Edit Text | **8** / **S** Shape | **3** Edit Image | |

**Esc** now steps down through whatever there is to cancel and, with nothing left, returns to the Select tool. (It still never quits the app.)

### Freeform polygons (new in 1.19.0.0)
The Shape tool gains a fourth kind next to Rectangle, Ellipse and Line. Click to place each vertex, double-click or click the highlighted first point to close, **Backspace** removes the last point, **Esc** cancels. Polygons share the shape bar's color, size, opacity and Fill toggle.

### Export pages as images (new in 1.19.0.0)
**File ▸ Export Pages as Images…** renders pages to PNG or JPEG at a chosen DPI (24–1200, default 150) with an optional page range. Pending annotations are burned in and in-app rotation is honored. Long exports show progress and cancel with **Esc**.

### Read in the dark (new in 1.19.0.0)
A moon toggle at the bottom of the sidebar rail (**Ctrl+I**) inverts the document's colors for comfortable dark-mode reading, remembered across launches. It is display-only: saving, printing, exporting, OCR and the thumbnails all keep the document's true colors.

### Scale the app to fit your eyes (new in 1.19.0.0)
Scale the toolbar, sidebar and tab strip from 70% to 250% with **Ctrl+Shift+=** / **Ctrl+Shift+-** / **Ctrl+Shift+0**, or by scrolling over the title-bar logo or the footer size chip. Remembered across launches. The document pane is deliberately untouched — app size and page zoom stay separate controls.

### Odd/even printing, and Remove Password (new in 1.19.0.0)
- **All pages / Odd only / Even only** in the print dialog, applied on top of the page range, with the preview following along. Print the odds, flip the stack, print the evens.
- **File ▸ Remove Password…** saves a protected document back over the original with its protection dropped. TDPdf has always written unprotected PDFs (the editing pipeline can't modify encrypted files in place) — this makes it a deliberate, visible action instead of a silent one.

## Fixes

- **Exported JPEGs came out as solid black pages.** PDFium leaves unpainted background transparent and JPEG has no alpha channel, so most PDFs exported black. Exports now composite over white — which also keeps a pointless full-page alpha channel out of flattened PDFs.
- **Form fields sat about 40 points out of place on US Letter and other non-A4 documents**, and PDF links had the same defect plus an unapplied page rotation. Both now resolve the page box the same way — CropBox over MediaBox, inherited through the page tree, with the box origin honored.
- **Saving could plant a zero-size `/MediaBox`** that Adobe rejects as "page dimensions out-of-range". Files damaged by an earlier build heal when re-saved.
- **Ctrl+S could write to a temporary file instead of your document** — after opening a password-protected file, after any structural edit (rotate, delete, reorder, crop), or after a repair. The save appeared to succeed, cleared the dirty flag, and the temp was deleted on exit. Saves now always target the real document.
- **Cropping retargeted the document to a stray `<name>.crop-<guid>.pdf`**, renaming the tab and adding that file to recents.
- **Delete and the arrow keys hijacked typing** in the find bar, the page-jump box and form fields — Delete could remove a page instead of a character.
- Inverted display colors could be baked into a saved PDF through the image-edit region capture.
- The sidebar now glides shut instead of snapping, starts collapsed on an empty workspace, and opens itself when you open a document.
- The **Password Required** prompt is now a properly themed dialog instead of a stock Windows one, and menu items carry their toolbar glyph — with real check marks for the items that carry state.

## Known gaps

- **Flowing selection is single-page.** Continuous view and cross-page selection are not covered; the classic behavior is unchanged there. TDPdf has one annotation canvas bound to the primary page while upstream keeps a live overlay per rendered page — extending this is a rendering change, and it was left out rather than shipped half-working.
- **Highlighting a scan still draws a rectangle.** Upstream replaced that gesture with a hint, having moved it into its Shapes tool; TDPdf's Shape tool never inherited it, so Highlight keeps the rectangle on a text-free page and says why in the status bar.
- Upstream's Czech/Japanese localization and its stamp fixes don't apply here — TDPdf is English-only and has no page-number/watermark stamping.
